hints.content:
The basic function $\sin(x)$ intersects its midline at $(0,0)$ and has a maximum point at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/06941548a579199b78346bf8e7ed0476.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\blue{5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} x-\pi\right)+3}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\green{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} x\right)}$ is a horizontal shrink by a factor of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so the maximum point's horizontal distance from the origin is shrunk from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{2}{\pi}=1$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} x\right)}$ to $\red{5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} x\right)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $5$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $5$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one, one).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (one, five).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} x\right)}$ to $\blue{5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} x-\pi\right)+3}$, which is equivalent to $5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} (x-2)\right)+3$, is a translation to the right by $2$ units and a translation upwards by $3$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the intersection point with the midline is now at $\left(2,3\right)$ and the maximum point is at $(3,8)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by one and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (two, three) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (three, eight).

question.content:
**Graph $f(x)=5\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} x-\pi\right)+3$ in the interactive widget.**  
*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
